title: City Lights
review: Still no bigger tearjerker! Chaplin is amazing!

title: Beauty and the Beast
review: This is what comes to mind when I think of Beauty and the Beast, rather than the Disney film. The surreal visuals surprised me.

title: The Third Man
review: The direction, visuals and music are still burned into my brain. I'd mistakenly thought until I grew up that Orson Welles directed it.

title: Singin' in the Rain
review: I like the Hollywood musicals of the "good old days", and this is my favorite. When I was a kid, I was in love with this period of America.

title: The Wages of Fear
review: The extreme realism shocked me. It's got its own Mario and Luigi. Yves Montand has great presence.

title: 12 Angry Men
review: This film made me think about just how inaccurate one's assumptions and stereotypes can be. It also was my first exposure to the American jury system.

title: Kanal
review: Most people would probably pick Ashes and Diamonds as their favorite of Wajda's films, but I like this one the best. It had a big influence on MGS, too.

title: The Pink Panther
review: My favorite comedic actor is the late Peter Sellers. I like nearly all of Edwards's and Sellers's films together, though the Pink Panther films are the best. This is where MGS gets its sense of humor.

title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
review: A bittersweet film. Catherine Deneuve is cute. This type of love story, where circumstances keep two people apart, really gets to me.

title: Fantastic Voyage
review: This never gets old for me. A popcorn movie, it combines science fiction and espionage to great effect. The art direction and special effects depicting the inner workings of the human body are not only amazing but scientifically accurate as well.

title: Somewhere in Time
review: I adore Richard Matheson's original novel and this movie, which he also wrote. Jane Seymour is really beautiful. I'm a sucker for this type of romance movie. John Barry's music is good, too.

title: Das Boot
review: This is my favorite submarine film. It's a powerful depiction of a group of men in extreme circumstances.

title: Mauvais Sang
review: I really like Carax, and this is my favorite work of his. It's a cool movie.

title: A Better Tomorrow II
review: This is one of my favorite John Woo films, right up there with Hard-Boiled. I still cry every time I watch it.

title: Fantastic Planet
review: The originality of its world and style left me speechless.

title: Wicked City
review: One of Mr. Kawajiri's best works. I respect him very much. It has an unrivaled speed to it! Seeing it now, it's like watching The Matrix.

title: Crayon Shin-chan: The Storm Called: The Adult Empire Strikes Back
review: A tearful, painful yet inspiring film for my generation. Anyone who writes it off as just a kids' movie is making a big mistake. It's an amazing film that a family can enjoy together, laughing, crying, cherishing.

title: Yojimbo
review: One of my favorite Kurosawa films, along with High and Low and Seven Samurai.

title: Asobi
review: This is based on Akiyuki Nosaka's novel. It's not the best of Masumura's films, but I just like it a lot for some reason. I was a fan of Keiko Sekine when I was a kid.

title: Castle of Sand
review: It has incredible direction, and moved and amazed me in ways the book didn't, in ways only film can. Yasushi Akutagawa's music is wonderful, too.

title: Burst City
review: This is Sogo Ishii's greatest work!! It has fantastic energy and soul! Mr. Ishii is my mentor in spirit. When I first saw this I thought, I want to be like him some day!

title: Night and Fog
review: This documentary belongs in my top thirty list. It's based on Viktor Frankl's novel Man's Search for Meaning, which my father made me read as a kid as well.

title: Casablanca
review: I didn't really understand what this was about when I was a kid, but the ending, the music and especially Ingrid Bergman's beauty (my mother was a big fan of her) are forever etched in my memory.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Thing from Another World
review: Carpenter's 1982 remake The Thing had an impact on me as well, but Howard Hawks's original is also a good film. Its outstanding direction on a low budget makes it a must-watch.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Elevator to the Gallows
review: Malle's masterpiece. This left a big impression on me when I saw it on TV. I'll never forget the music.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Fabulous World of Jules Verne
review: Watching it now I'm still blown away by how its world was created. The special effects, all done by hand and accomplishing things you can't do with CG, are amazing.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Jason and the Argonauts
review: This is my favorite of all Ray Harryhausen's films.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Alphaville
review: I doubt many people would single out this film from Godard's works (I also like Breathless), but I'm fond of it.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: One Million Years B.C.
review: The dinosaurs were incredible in this. This film overstimulated my very young mind. Another movie from Hammer Films.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Last Adventure
review: When I was a kid, I thought the strange relationship between the three main characters was cool.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Barbarella
review: Erotic and kitsch sci-fi humor. The young Jane Fonda is amazing.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
review: Katharine Ross is so innocent in this. Burt Bacharach's songs are good, too. The ending really hits hard.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: El Topo
review: A two-part film that's acquired a cult following. The way the boss characters appear one-by-one and reveal their beliefs had quite an influence on MGS.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Silent Running
review: The designs and movements of the drone robots Huey, Dewey and Louie are cute. While a little plain, it has an outstanding story.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Spirit of the Beehive
review: Ana Torrent is adorable as the child. I'm also a sucker for films starring children.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Papillon
review: It had an influence on MGS, along with The Great Escape, because of the concept of "escape". The look on Dustin Hoffman's face at the end is great. So is Jerry Goldsmith's music.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Towering Inferno
review: A masterful disaster film. Just like Dawn of the Dead, its closed environments influenced MGS, particularly the use of elevators, shafts, ducts and stairs.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Rollerball
review: This was the first film I went to see at a movie theater by myself, at the OS Theater in Osaka. I have a lot of memories of this film.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Bullet Train
review: A Japanese disaster film masterpiece. Not only does it have an interesting story and suspense, it feels real.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Cassandra Crossing
review: A classic from the peak of the disaster film era. Its all-star cast, the suspense on the train and its big set-piece at the end are its highlights. Goldsmith's music is also good.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Alien
review: Cameron's Aliens is a classic in its own right, but I prefer the first one. When I saw it when it was released, I was shaking in my seat with dread.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Right Stuff
review: A must-see for anyone who's into astronauts.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: The Name of the Rose
review: Its 14th century world, as well as the art direction and cinematography, are incredible.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Bad Taste
review: This also inspired MGS's humor — jokes that dissolve tension — with scenes like the puking in the alien base.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

title: Die Hard
review: A classic from the height of McTiernan's career. It has great direction and camerawork, in addition to a solid story with good use of foreshadowing. This had a huge influence on '90s action films.

sources.label: My Favorite Films — Runners-Up (MGS Naked Essay)

review: My favorite Luc Besson film.
